purpose: Continue raw coverage through 99369, 93996, 69993, 69399, 93599, 95939, 99953 and 99335 while routing relativistic-plasma, microwave-heating and spectroscopy-related sources into Worldshepherd.

policy.rule: Raw repository, CID, CAS, PII, affiliation and count occurrences have zero automatic physical-evidence weight.
policy.promotion: Counts, identifiers and addresses are not P1 even when they occur inside experimental physics papers; P1 requires the five digits to encode the verified physical quantity itself.
policy.source_quality: Derivative snippets may seed a raw candidate, but primary or authoritative source resolution is required before evidence promotion.

information_updates.finding: The microwave-powder paper provides a quantitative EM-heating design rule: highly conducting particles are dominated by magnetic-induction absorption, with optimum particle radius tied to skin depth, whereas weak conductors can be electric-dipole dominated.
information_updates.claims_boundary: 93996 is a repository ID, not a measured absorption value.

information_updates.finding: The relativistic-plasma paper derives a surface-integral representation for electric intensity when tangential electromagnetic fields and the electronic distribution function are specified on the enclosing surface; use as an EM/plasma boundary-formulation reference.

The 69399 cluster demonstrates high within-prefix collision multiplicity in chemical registries: one target can match a PubChem CID and several distinct CAS prefixes while remaining entirely metadata-level.
Experimental data counts such as 99335 crystallographic reflections must remain distinct from measured physical quantities; they can characterize dataset scale but do not satisfy P1.

next_actions: Run physical-value searches independently and do not promote experimental data counts, addresses or identifiers.
Use source-namespace and leading-zero strata in collision-density/null modeling.
Maintain fixed tolerance and experiment-wide multiple-testing/false-discovery correction for physical evidence.
